program.name: Boy Scouts Handbook 1911
program.description: The merit badges in the Boy Scouts Handbook, First Edition, 1911 (Boy Scouts of America), as printed then. Historical 1911 text, not a current or official Scouting America requirement. Many of these badges are obsolete or unsafe today. You do not need to do anything unsafe. Ask a trusted adult before you try any requirement, and skip what you cannot do safely. The wording, spelling and punctuation are kept as printed. This app is unofficial and is not recognized by Scouting America. Source: Project Gutenberg eBook #29558. The book is in the US public domain because of its age. If you live outside the US, check your local law.

requirements.text: Demonstrate riding at a walk, trot, and gallop.
Know how to saddle and bridle a horse correctly.
Know how to water and feed and to what amount, and how to groom a horse properly.
Know how to harness a horse correctly in single or double harness and to drive.
Have a knowledge of the power of endurance of horses at work and know the local regulations concerning driving.
Know the management and care of horses.
Be able to identify unsoundness and blemishes.
Know the evils of bearing or check reins and of ill-fitting harness or saddlery.
Know two common causes of, and proper remedies for, lameness, and know to whom he should refer cases of cruelty and abuse.
Be able to judge as to the weight, height, and age of horses; know three breeds and their general characteristics.
